newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Quick assessing Burger King French move.
newsitem.headline: Quick assessing Burger King French move.

text.p: Belgian fast food chain Quick said on Tuesday it was assessing the implications for itself of competitor Burger King's decision to pull out of France.
"They have only a few restaurants that could interest us and we are right now evaluating the real interest for us," a spokesman told Reuters.
"Some of them are in direct competition with us, so there are only really a couple that might be of interest," he added.
Burger King, owned by Britain's Grand Metropolitan Plc, said on Tuesday it planned to withdraw from France.
"Burger King doesn't have a critical mass in the French market. It had to make the announcement now because of the unions and labour laws," the Quick spokesman said.
Burger King has a total 39 restaurants in France, mainly in and around Paris, 16 of these are company owned with the remainder owned by franchisees.
Most of the franchised outlets will cease trading as Burger King by December 31, the company said in a statement issued in London.
